title: AI Visibility Tools: Compared by Plan Caps (2026)
summary: AI visibility tools track where ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google's AI mention your brand. Compare pricing and limits to pick the right tool.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces


**Nothing in Activepieces tracks AI visibility** , so it earns its place as the thing you run after a tracker, not instead of one. Flows are unlimited on every plan, including the free one, so adding a follow-up job never means buying a bigger tier.


As a workflow automation tool, Activepieces connects apps, runs on a schedule or a trigger, and moves data between them, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


It doesn't query ChatGPT or any other engine, and it won't tell you whether a brand was mentioned.


Every number it handles has to come from a tracker you already pay for.


### Where it fits and where it does not


Telling you when something changed, in the place your team already looks, is the one job most trackers do badly. A tracker's dashboard shows citations, but someone has to open it.


Activepieces can fetch the figures on a timer, compare them and push a message, so the numbers reach you without a login. At 1 credit per run, a weekly check uses about four or five of the free plan's 1,000 monthly credits.


Whether this works depends on the tracker exposing the data. If your plan offers an API or a scheduled export, the workflow is straightforward.


If the plan only gives you a dashboard, there's nothing to pull, and you'd be scraping a page, which I wouldn't build on. Check that before you commit to either tool.


On integrations, Slack and Google Sheets are among the 744 integrations counted in Activepieces' MIT-licensed open source monorepo, so those steps are configuration, not code.


Expect to reach most AI visibility trackers through an HTTP request step or a webhook, since they are unlikely to have a dedicated integration.


That works, but you handle authentication, pagination and response shapes yourself, and a change in the tracker's API breaks your flow quietly.


### A weekly visibility report workflow in outline


Short enough to build in an afternoon, the sequence below shows the whole loop from pull to alert to record, and the thing to take from it is that only step two depends on your tracker.


1. Set a schedule trigger to run once a week.
2. Pull the tracker's export or API data for the period.
3. Compare this week's citation count with last week's.
4. If citations dropped, post an alert to a Slack channel.
5. Append a row to a Google Sheet, whether or not there was a drop.


Step five is what makes the rest useful. The sheet gives you a running history, and last week's figure for step three can be read back from it. Once that history exists, you can judge whether a drop is a trend or noise.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams that run multi-step follow-up automations after an AI visibility tracker has done the measuring, judged on how the bill scales as workflows grow.


Its published pricing meters the run, at 1 credit per flow run regardless of how many steps sit inside it, whereas Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so every added step in those tools adds to the meter.


It won't track brand mentions or query any engine, so it complements a tracker rather than replacing one, but for the automation layer that comes after, the cost stays predictable as flows get longer.
